punchline: Rowling didn't find more willpower to finish Harry Potter. She found a hotel room.
thirty_sec: While writing the final Harry Potter book, J.K. Rowling couldn't concentrate at home because of children, household activity and constant interruptions. So she checked into a suite at the Balmoral, a luxury hotel in Edinburgh, and finished Deathly Hallows there. Cal Newport calls this a 'grand gesture.' The cost and effort of the move made the work feel more important, and that made procrastination harder. It worked because she changed the setting instead of trying harder.
question: If your most important project were worth spending real money on to finish, what would you change about where and how you work on it?
